sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你不仅能聆听引人入胜的故事，探索世界上光怪陆离的奇妙事物，还能顺便提升英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the Salem Witch Trials.
sentences.zh: 我是阿莱斯特·巴奇（Alastair Budge），今天我们要聊一聊塞勒姆审巫案（The Salem Witch Trials）。

sentences.en: It’s a story of suspicion, the devil, witchcraft– alleged witchcraft, I should add–mass hysteria, hints of psychedelic drugs, and justice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满猜疑、恶魔、巫术——我得补充一下，是所谓的巫术——群体歇斯底里、迷幻药痕迹以及正义的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s step into the icy, unsettling world of the Salem Witch Trials.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们走进塞勒姆审巫案那冰冷、令人不安的世界吧。

sentences.en: The winter of 1692 was particularly cold in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 1692年的冬天在马萨诸塞州异常寒冷。

sentences.en: The temperature rarely got above freezing point, and many of the ponds and rivers had been frozen over since late the previous year.
sentences.zh: 气温很少升至冰点以上，许多池塘和河流从前一年的年末起就一直结着厚冰。

sentences.en: In the small village of Salem, the 500 or so Puritan settlers did everything they could to stay warm.
sentences.zh: 在塞勒姆这个仅有约500名清教徒定居的小村庄里，大家想尽一切办法来保暖。

sentences.en: Church was, of course, a regular occurrence.
sentences.zh: 当然，做礼拜是必不可少的常规活动。

sentences.en: This was a highly religious community. And what these god-fearing men and women feared the most was, naturally, the devil.
sentences.zh: 这是一个宗教氛围极浓的社群。这些敬畏上帝的男女最恐惧的，自然就是魔鬼。

sentences.en: In Salem Village, the devil wasn’t just a story whispered to scare children; he was real.
sentences.zh: 在塞勒姆村，魔鬼可不仅仅是用来吓唬小孩子的睡前故事；他是真实存在的。

sentences.en: To the 500 or so Puritans huddled in their icy wooden homes, he was an ever-present enemy, lurking in the shadows, waiting to snatch their souls.
sentences.zh: 对于挤在冰冷木屋里的那大约500名清教徒来说，他是无处不在的敌人，潜伏在阴影中，随时准备夺走他们的灵魂。

sentences.en: But why were they so afraid? Why did this small, God-fearing community see the devil behind every misfortune?
sentences.zh: 但他们为什么会如此恐惧？为什么这个小小的、敬畏上帝的社群会在每一次不幸背后都看到魔鬼的影子？

sentences.en: Well, these settlers weren’t just a random collection of English people, they were Puritans, a group so strict, so devoted, that they’d crossed an ocean to build a ‘pure’ life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些定居者可不是随便拼凑的一群英国人，他们是清教徒，一个极其严格、极其虔诚的群体，他们跨越大洋，只为了建立一种“纯净”的生活。

sentences.en: Back in England, their parents or grandparents had watched the Protestant Reformation unfold, and they believed the Church of England, the Protestant church, hadn’t gone far enough to strip away Catholic influences.
sentences.zh: 在英国老家，他们的父辈或祖辈见证了新教改革的展开，他们认为英国国教——也就是新教教会——做得还不够彻底，未能彻底清除天主教的影响。

sentences.en: So they sailed across the Atlantic, dreaming of a holy community, a shining “city upon a hill”.
sentences.zh: 于是他们扬帆起航跨越大西洋，怀揣着建立一个圣洁社群、打造一座闪耀的“山巅之城”的梦想。

sentences.en: But that dream came with a catch: if they were God’s chosen people, and of course, they fervently believed that they were, the devil would surely try to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 但这个梦想有个前提：既然他们是上帝的选民——当然，他们狂热地坚信这一点——那么魔鬼必定会千方百计地摧毁他们。

sentences.en: And in early 1692, life gave them plenty of reasons to feel that the devil was edging closer.
sentences.zh: 而在1692年初，生活给他们提供了充足的理由，让他们觉得魔鬼正在步步逼近。

sentences.en: The winter was brutal, crops had failed, smallpox had swept through, and Indian raids from the north had left families grieving.
sentences.zh: 冬天残酷无情，庄稼绝收，天花肆虐，北方的印第安人袭击更是让许多家庭陷入失去亲人的悲痛之中。

sentences.en: Every creak of the floorboards, every howl of the wind through the frozen trees, felt like a sign.
sentences.zh: 地板的每一次吱呀作响，风吹过冰冻树林时的每一次呼啸，都感觉像是一种征兆。

sentences.en: The Puritans believed the devil wasn’t some distant figure, someone you might meet in hell if you didn’t live a god-fearing life; he was here, or rather, his secret servants were.
sentences.zh: 清教徒相信，魔鬼并不是什么遥不可及的人物，不是那种如果你生活不够敬畏上帝就会在地狱里见到的角色；他就这里，或者说，他的秘密仆从就在这里。

sentences.en: These servants were witches, people, almost exclusively women, who had made a pact with Satan, a deal with the devil.
sentences.zh: 这些仆从就是女巫，也就是几乎全为女性的人，她们与撒旦立了契约，与魔鬼做了交易。

sentences.en: And they weren’t random strangers; they were neighbours, friends, even family, who were working with the devil.
sentences.zh: 而且她们不是什么素不相识的陌生人；她们是邻居、朋友，甚至是亲人，却在与魔鬼勾结。

sentences.en: His tricks were clever: he could send ‘ spectres,’ invisible spirits, to pinch or choke you in the night.
sentences.zh: 他的伎俩非常高明：他可以派遣“幽灵”（即无形的精魂）在夜里掐你或勒你。

sentences.en: He could turn your cow’s milk sour or make your children fall ill and die.
sentences.zh: 他能让你家母牛的奶变酸，或者让你的孩子生病夭折。

sentences.en: Every Sunday, Reverend Samuel Parris, the village minister, would stand in front of his congregation and preach exactly this.
sentences.zh: 每个星期天，村里的牧师塞缪尔·帕里斯（Samuel Parris）都会站在会众面前，宣讲的正是这些内容。

sentences.en: Beware the devil; he has evil and cunning ways, and he is sending witches to test you.
sentences.zh: 警惕魔鬼；他诡计多端、阴险狡诈，正派遣女巫来考验你们。

sentences.en: Perhaps it all sounded theoretical, but in January of 1692, he noticed something unusual happening in his own house.
sentences.zh: 也许这一切听起来很理论化，但在1692年1月，他在自己的家里发现了一些异常情况。

sentences.en: His daughter, Betty, and her cousin Abigail, started behaving strangely.
sentences.zh: 他的女儿贝蒂（Betty）和侄女阿比盖尔（Abigail）开始举止怪异。

sentences.en: They were only 9 and 11 years old, but suddenly, they weren’t acting like children anymore.
sentences.zh: 她们当时只有9岁和11岁，但突然之间，她们看起来一点也不像小孩子了。

sentences.en: They twitched and shook, cried out in pain, and complained of being pinched or bitten.
sentences.zh: 她们抽搐颤抖，痛苦哭喊，抱怨自己被掐或被咬。

sentences.en: But there was nothing there. It wasn’t mice, it wasn’t some pest, or bed bugs.
sentences.zh: 但周围什么也没有。不是老鼠，不是什么害虫，也不是臭虫。

sentences.en: They seemed to be being attacked by some invisible force.
sentences.zh: 她们似乎正受到某种看不见的力量的攻击。

sentences.en: At first, it might have seemed like a sickness.
sentences.zh: 起初，这可能看起来像是一场病。

sentences.en: After all, the winter had been harsh, and disease wasn’t uncommon.
sentences.zh: 毕竟冬天很严酷，生病并不罕见。

sentences.en: But when a local doctor examined them and found no clear cause, he gave an altogether different explanation: witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但当当地医生为她们检查却找不到明确病因时，他给出了一个完全不同的解释：巫术。

sentences.en: To the Puritans, this made perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 对清教徒来说，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: If the devil was real, and his witches were among them, then these girls were under attack.
sentences.zh: 如果魔鬼是真实的，而且他的女巫就在他们中间，那么这些女孩显然受到了攻击。

sentences.en: Word spread quickly through the village.
sentences.zh: 消息迅速在村里传开。

sentences.en: Salem was small, only about 500 people, so news travelled fast, from house to house, whispered over fences and church pews.
sentences.zh: 塞勒姆很小，只有大约500人，所以消息传播得极快，挨家挨户，在篱笆和教堂长椅旁低声耳语。

sentences.en: Soon, other girls in the village started showing the same signs.
sentences.zh: 很快，村里的其他女孩也开始表现出同样的症状。

sentences.en: Ann Putnam Jr., a 12-year-old from a powerful family, and Mercy Lewis, a 17-year-old servant, joined Betty and Abigail in their fits.
sentences.zh: 小安妮·普特南（Ann Putnam Jr.），一个来自显赫家庭的12岁女孩，以及17岁的女佣默西·刘易斯（Mercy Lewis），也加入了贝蒂和阿比盖尔的抽搐行列。

sentences.en: They screamed about invisible tormentors, pointed fingers, and named names.
sentences.zh: 她们尖叫着谈论那些看不见的折磨者，指指点点，并说出具体的名字。

sentences.en: The first to be accused were the kind of people you might expect in a suspicious little village: outcasts, people on the edges.
sentences.zh: 第一批被指控的人正是你在一个充满猜忌的小村庄里所能预料到的那种人：边缘人、被排挤者。

sentences.en: There was Sarah Good, a beggar who smoked a pipe and muttered under her breath when anyone refused her charity.
sentences.zh: 其中有萨拉·古德（Sarah Good），一个抽着烟斗的乞丐，当别人拒绝她的施舍时，她会在嘴里嘟嘟囔囔。

sentences.en: Then Sarah Osborne, an older woman who’d shocked the village by marrying her servant and committing the most scandalous crime of all: skipping church.
sentences.zh: 还有萨拉·奥斯本（Sarah Osborne），一个年长的妇女，她嫁给了自己的仆人，这震惊了整个村庄，并且犯下了最骇人听闻的罪行：逃去不做礼拜。

sentences.en: And finally, Tituba, a black slave woman who worked in Reverend Parris’s own home.
sentences.zh: 最后是蒂图芭（Tituba），一个在帕里斯牧师家中工作的黑人女奴。

sentences.en: Now, not much is known about Tituba. It’s thought she might have come from the Caribbean, perhaps Haiti, and if so, she may well have told the girls stories about Voodoo, spirits and fortune-telling.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们对蒂图芭知之甚少。据推测她可能来自加勒比海，或许是海地，如果是这样，她很可能给女孩们讲过关于伏都教、神灵和算命的故事。

sentences.en: These might have sounded weird and fascinating, but with the accusation of witchcraft, to her Puritan master, they sounded like the work of the devil.
sentences.zh: 这些听起来可能既古怪又迷人，但在她清教徒主人看来，伴随着巫术的指控，这些就成了魔鬼的恶行。

sentences.en: Under pressure, Tituba confessed. She was questioned for days, beaten, and likely told that confessing could save her life, while denying it would mean death.
sentences.zh: 在压力之下，蒂图芭招供了。她被审讯了好几天，遭到殴打，很可能有人告诉她，认罪能救她一命，而否认则意味着死路一条。

sentences.en: In a village gripped by fear, she had little choice but to give them what they wanted: a story.
sentences.zh: 在一个被恐惧笼罩的小村庄里，她别无选择，只能给他们想要的答案：一个故事。

sentences.en: She described visions of black dogs, red cats, and witches flying through the air, details that matched Puritan fears perfectly.
sentences.zh: 她描述了自己看到的幻象：黑狗、红猫，以及在空中飞行的女巫，这些细节完美契合了清教徒的恐惧。

sentences.en: She said she’d met the devil, that he’d asked her to serve him, and that she’d seen other witches in Salem signing his book, a sort of evil guest list.
sentences.zh: 她说她见过魔鬼，魔鬼要求她侍奉他，她还看到塞勒姆的其他女巫在魔鬼的册子上签名，那简直就像是一份邪恶的来宾名单。

sentences.en: Her confession wasn’t just a story; it was fuel.
sentences.zh: 她的供词不仅仅是一个故事，更是火上浇油。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the village had proof, or so they thought.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，全村人都有了证据——他们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: If Tituba was a witch, then the girls’ fits weren’t imagination; they were evidence.
sentences.zh: 如果蒂图芭是个女巫，那么女孩们的抽搐就不是凭空想象，而是铁证。

sentences.en: And if there were more witches out there, as Tituba claimed, no one was safe.
sentences.zh: 而且正如蒂图芭所说，如果外面还有更多女巫，那就没有人是安全的了。

sentences.en: Soon, fingers started to be pointed every which way.
sentences.zh: 很快，人们开始四处指指点点。

sentences.en: The accusations didn’t stop with the outcasts.
sentences.zh: 指控并没有止步于边缘人群。

sentences.en: They spread to people no one expected: a 71-year-old grandmother who went to church every Sunday and a well-respected farmer.
sentences.zh: 它们蔓延到了意想不到的人身上：一个每个星期天都去教堂的71岁祖母，以及一个备受尊敬的农夫。

sentences.en: When a woman named Martha Corey, who was in her 70s at the time, dared to question if the girls were telling the truth, she found herself accused of being a witch.
sentences.zh: 当一个名叫玛莎·科里（Martha Corey）的70多岁老妇人敢于质疑这些女孩是否在说实话时，她发现自己也被指控为女巫。

sentences.en: Her husband, Giles Corey, an 80-year-old farmer, was another one of the few who refused to play along, and of course, he found himself accused of witchcraft too.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫吉尔斯·科里（Giles Corey），一个80岁的农夫，是为数不多拒绝随波逐流的人之一，理所当然地，他也发现自己被指控犯有巫术罪。

sentences.en: He wouldn’t confess or deny the charges, so the court ordered him to be pressed under heavy stones, a terrible torture intended to get him to realise the error of his ways and corroborate.
sentences.zh: 他既不认罪也不否认指控，于是法庭下令用重石压在他身上，这是一种残酷的刑罚，旨在让他认识到自己的错误并供认不讳。

sentences.en: For two days, he lay there, saying only ‘More weight,’ until he died, a stubborn stand against the madness.
sentences.zh: 他躺在那里整整两天，嘴里只念叨着“再加点重量”，直到死去，这是对狂热的顽强抵抗。

sentences.en: His wife was executed three days later. In a village of 500, where everyone knew each other, this had become personal.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子三天后被处决。在一个只有500人、彼此熟识的村庄里，这一切已经变得极其私人化。

sentences.en: Neighbour turned against neighbour, enemy against enemy, friend against friend.
sentences.zh: 邻居反目成仇，仇敌互相攻讦，朋友分道扬镳。

sentences.en: By spring, the panic had grown so big that the local magistrates couldn’t handle it anymore.
sentences.zh: 到了春天，恐慌情绪扩散得如此之大，以至于当地治安官再也无法控制局面了。

sentences.en: A special court was set up in Salem Town, just a few miles away, to deal with the growing list of the accused.
sentences.zh: 一个特别法庭在几英里外的塞勒姆镇设立，专门处理日益增多的被指控人员名单。

sentences.en: And here’s where things got even stranger: the court didn’t rely on normal evidence, like witnesses or proof you could touch.
sentences.zh: 接下来事情变得更加离奇：法庭不依赖常规证据，比如证人或你可以触摸得到的物证。

sentences.en: They used ‘ spectral evidence’, the idea that the devil could send a witch’s spirit to harm someone, even if her body were somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 他们使用“幽灵证据”，即这样一种观点：即使某个女巫的肉身在别处，魔鬼也可以派遣她的灵魂去伤害别人。

sentences.en: If a girl screamed in court and said she saw Sarah Good’s spectre choking her, that was enough.
sentences.zh: 如果一个女孩在法庭上尖叫，说她看见萨拉·古德的幽灵在掐她，这就足够了。

sentences.en: It didn’t matter if Sarah was standing right there, clearly not doing anything other than trying to defend herself.
sentences.zh: 至于萨拉就站在那里、明明除了试图辩护外什么也没做，这根本不重要。

sentences.en: To the Puritans, the invisible world was just as real as the frozen ponds outside.
sentences.zh: 在清教徒看来，无形的世界和外面结冰的池塘一样真实。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, the courtroom was a mess: girls fainting, judges pushing for guilty verdicts, and even a ‘touch test’ where if an accused touched a girl and her fits stopped, it was proof of guilt.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，法庭上一团糟：女孩们昏厥，法官极力推动有罪判决，甚至还有一种“触摸测试”，如果被指控的人碰了一下女孩而女孩的抽搐停止了，这就成了有罪的证据。

sentences.en: By summer, the jails were full, and the gallows were busy.
sentences.zh: 到了夏天，监狱里人满为患，绞刑架忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: Nineteen people were hanged that year. Five more died in prison, including Sarah Osborne, who was worn out by illness and chains.
sentences.zh: 那一年有十九人被绞死。另有五人在狱中死去，其中包括因疾病和锁链折磨而油尽灯枯的萨拉·奥斯本。

sentences.en: And Giles Corey, of course, met his end under the stones.
sentences.zh: 而吉尔斯·科里当然也在乱石重压下走向了生命的终点。

sentences.en: But it couldn’t go on forever. By late summer, the accusations had become a form of village retribution, a way to settle scores with quarrelling neighbours.
sentences.zh: 但这不可能永远持续下去。到了夏末，指控已经演变成一种村庄内部的报复手段，成了与争吵不休的邻居了结恩怨的方式。

sentences.en: If there was a dispute over land or some feeling of being wronged in the past, what better way to get your vengeance than accusing your enemy of being in bed with the devil?
sentences.zh: 如果存在土地纠纷或者过去遭受过某种委屈，还有什么比指控你的仇敌与魔鬼同床共枕更好的复仇方式呢？

sentences.en: In fact, it took the accusations to reach the very top of Puritan society for the madness to end.
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到指控波及到清教徒社会的最高层，这场疯狂才终于结束。

sentences.en: People began pointing fingers at the wives of important men, like the wife of Governor William Phips, who was in charge of Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 人们开始把矛头指向大人物的妻子，比如负责马萨诸塞事务的威廉·菲普斯（William Phips）总督的夫人。

sentences.en: This was a step too far. Phips had been away, dealing with Indian wars up north, but when he returned in October 1692, he saw the chaos and shut the special court down.
sentences.zh: 这未免太过分了。菲普斯一直在北方处理印第安战争，但当他于1692年10月返回时，他看到了这片混乱，并下令关闭了特别法庭。

sentences.en: Or, more cynically, he might have thought, “I don’t mind people accusing other people’s wives of being a witch, but you’re not going to accuse my wife of witchcraft!”
sentences.zh: 或者，更刻薄一点地说，他当时的想法可能是：“我不在乎别人指控别人的妻子是女巫，但你们休想诬陷我老婆是巫婆！”

sentences.en: He banned spectral evidence, saying it wasn’t reliable.
sentences.zh: 他禁止使用幽灵证据，称其不可靠。

sentences.en: Of course, it wasn’t reliable; it was invisible and was one person’s word against another's.
sentences.zh: 当然，这本就不可靠；它虚无缥缈，而且完全是各执一词。

sentences.en: Without that, most of the cases fell apart because there was no evidence.
sentences.zh: 没有了这些，大部分案件都由于缺乏证据而土崩瓦解。

sentences.en: The trials slowed, then stopped. By early 1693, the jails started to empty.
sentences.zh: 审判慢了下来，随后停滞。到了1693年初，监狱开始空了。

sentences.en: Tituba, who’d confessed, was sold to a new owner and disappeared from the records.
sentences.zh: 曾经认罪的蒂图芭被卖给了一位新主人，从此在记录中消失了。

sentences.en: The girls, Betty, Abigail, Ann and Mercy, went quiet, their fits fading away as the village tried to move on.
sentences.zh: 贝蒂、阿比盖尔、安妮和默西这些女孩也安静了下来，随着村庄试图向前看，她们的抽搐也渐渐消失了。

sentences.en: Years later, in 1706, Ann Putnam Jr. stood in church and apologised.
sentences.zh: 多年后的1706年，小安妮·普特南（Ann Putnam Jr.）站在教堂里公开道歉。

sentences.en: She said she’d been tricked–by the devil, she claimed–and hadn’t meant to hurt anyone.
sentences.zh: 她说自己当时受了蛊惑——她声称是魔鬼干的——并不是故意要伤害任何人。

sentences.en: By then, 20 people were dead, and Salem was a village full of scars.
sentences.zh: 到那时，已有20人丧生，塞勒姆成了一个满目疮痍的村庄。

sentences.en: In the immediate aftermath, there were movements to try to undo some of the damage, or at least acknowledge the sheer insanity of it.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的短期内，出现了一些试图弥补部分损失的行动，或者至少承认了那种彻头彻尾的疯狂。

sentences.en: In 1702, the trials were declared unlawful.
sentences.zh: 1702年，法庭的审判被宣布为非法。

sentences.en: Then, in 1711, the government passed a law to restore the rights and good names of many who’d been condemned.
sentences.zh: 接着在1711年，政府通过了一项法律，恢复了许多被定罪者的权利和好名声。

sentences.en: They even paid some money to the families, a token compensation payment by way of apology.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至向这些家庭支付了一些金钱，作为一种象征性的赔偿和道歉方式。

sentences.en: It wasn’t much, but it was something. Still, not everyone was included.
sentences.zh: 钱虽不多，总归是个表态。不过，并非所有人都被包含在内。

sentences.en: Seven people’s names stayed on the list of the guilty, forgotten by that first effort.
sentences.zh: 有七个人的名字留在了有罪名单上，被初期的那次努力所遗漏。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until 1957 that Massachusetts said sorry and tried to fix it again, clearing more names.
sentences.zh: 直到1957年，马萨诸塞州才正式道歉并试图再次纠正错误，为更多的人平反。

sentences.en: But one person, a woman named Elizabeth Johnson Jr., was somehow missed out.
sentences.zh: 但有一个人，一个名叫小伊丽莎白·约翰逊（Elizabeth Johnson Jr.）的妇女，却不知为何被遗漏了。

sentences.en: She’d been accused and convicted but not hanged.
sentences.zh: 她曾被指控并定罪，但没有被绞死。

sentences.en: She died of natural causes in 1747 at the ripe old age of 77 but with no living descendants to fight to clear her name, legally speaking, she was still a witch.
sentences.zh: 她在1747年以77岁的高龄寿终正寝，由于没有健在的后代来为她奔走平反，从法律上讲，她依然是个女巫。

sentences.en: However, more than 300 years after this conviction, she found some unlikely supporters in the form of a particularly creative teacher called Carrie LaPierre and her middle school class.
sentences.zh: 然而，在这场定罪300多年后，她找到了一些意料之外的支持者，其中包括一位极具创造力的教师卡丽·拉皮埃尔（Carrie LaPierre）和她所在的初中班级。

sentences.en: Mrs LaPierre found out about Elizabeth Johnson Jr and set her eighth-grade class a project: clear her name.
sentences.zh: 拉皮埃尔太太偶然发现了小伊丽莎白·约翰逊的事迹，于是给她的八年级学生布置了一个项目：为她平反。

sentences.en: The class worked tirelessly, collating records and writing letters, and in 2022, a bill was passed that officially exonerated Elizabeth Johnson Jr., thereby clearing the last convicted person in the Salem Witch Trials.
sentences.zh: 全班同学不知疲倦地工作，整理档案，写信求助，终于在2022年，一项法案通过了，正式宣布小伊丽莎白·约翰逊无罪，从而洗清了塞勒姆审巫案中最后一位被定罪者的罪名。

sentences.en: Of course, she should never have been convicted in the first place, but it was better than nothing, and Mrs LaPierre definitely deserves some sort of prize for devising such an interesting class project.
sentences.zh: 当然，她一开始就不该被定罪，但总比什么都没有强，拉皮埃尔太太绝对值得因为设计了这样一堂有趣的班级课题而获得某种奖励。

sentences.en: So, if we are to conclude that the residents of Salem were not being challenged by the devil, and there was not a mass transformation of the female population into witches, what was going on?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们认定塞勒姆的居民并没有受到魔鬼的挑衅，女性群体也没有大规模变身为女巫，那当时究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, people have been trying to figure that out for centuries, and there are a few theories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们几个世纪以来一直在试图弄清这一点，目前有几种假说。

sentences.en: One idea is that it all came down to a fungus.
sentences.zh: 其中一种观点认为，这一切归咎于一种真菌。

sentences.en: Ergot, to be exact. Ergot grows on rye, a grain the Puritans used to make bread.
sentences.zh: 确切地说，是麦角菌。麦角菌生长在黑麦上，而黑麦正是清教徒用来做面包的谷物。

sentences.en: If the weather is wet and warm, like it might have been in the summer of 1691, ergot can spread fast.
sentences.zh: 如果天气又湿又暖，就像1691年夏天那样，麦角菌就会迅速蔓延。

sentences.en: Now, here’s the strange part. Ergot contains natural chemicals that are similar to LSD, the powerful hallucinogenic drug that became famous in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 有趣的部分来了。麦角菌含有的天然化学物质类似于LSD，即在20世纪60年代名声大噪的强力致幻剂。

sentences.en: LSD causes people to see and feel things that aren’t real, and ergot can do something similar.
sentences.zh: LSD会让人看到和感觉到并不真实的东西，麦角菌也能起到类似的作用。

sentences.en: If someone eats bread made with infected rye, they might become very sick, have convulsions, feel like they’re being pinched or burned, or even see things that aren’t really there.
sentences.zh: 如果有人吃了用受感染黑麦做成的面包，他们可能会病得不轻、浑身抽搐、感觉自己被掐或被灼烧，甚至看到根本不存在的东西。

sentences.en: In other words, make people do exactly what the young girls did.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这会让人们做出和当年那些小女孩一模一样的举动。

sentences.en: Some historians think this could explain the strange behaviour, not witches, just bad bread.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，这可以解释那种奇异的行为，根本没有什么女巫，只是面包坏了而已。

sentences.en: But not everyone agrees. The symptoms don’t match perfectly, nor does the timeline, and ergot poisoning would’ve hit more people, not just a handful of girls.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有人都赞同这种说法。症状并不完全吻合，时间线也对不上，而且如果真是麦角菌中毒，受害者应该更多，而不仅仅是少数几个女孩。

sentences.en: Another theory is simpler: mass hysteria.
sentences.zh: 另一种理论更简单：群体歇斯底里。

sentences.en: Salem was a pressure cooker; harsh winters, failed crops, disease, and attacks from nearby tribes had nearly everyone on edge.
sentences.zh: 塞勒姆就像是一个高压锅；严冬、歉收、疾病以及来自周边部落的袭击，让几乎所有人都处于高度紧绷状态。

sentences.en: Add in their deep fear of the devil, and it wouldn’t have taken much to spark panic.
sentences.zh: 再加上他们对魔鬼的刻骨恐惧，只需要一点微小的火星就能引发恐慌。

sentences.en: When the girls started twitching and shouting, the village was ready to believe the worst.
sentences.zh: 当女孩们开始抽搐和尖叫时，全村人已经准备好往最坏的方向去想了。

sentences.en: Fear spread like wildfire, and soon, people saw witches everywhere because they expected to.
sentences.zh: 恐惧如野火般蔓延，很快，人们到处都能看到女巫，因为他们心中本就期待着女巫的出现。

sentences.en: The girls might have kept it going, maybe for attention, maybe out of fear themselves, while adults fuelled the flames with old grudges and power struggles.
sentences.zh: 女孩们可能一直在延续这种状况，也许是为了引起注意，也许是出于自身的恐惧，而成年人们则用陈年旧怨和权力争斗火上浇油。

sentences.en: Then there’s the idea of plain old jealousy and spite.
sentences.zh: 还有一种观点认为是纯粹的嫉妒和恶意。

sentences.en: Salem was tiny, 500 people, and everyone knew everyone else’s business.
sentences.zh: 塞勒姆极其渺小，只有500人，每个人都对别人的私事了如指掌。

sentences.en: Sarah Good was poor and bitter; Sarah Osborne broke the rules; Tituba was an outsider.
sentences.zh: 萨拉·古德又穷又尖酸；萨拉·奥斯本打破了常规；蒂图芭是个局外人。

sentences.en: Accusing them could settle scores or shift blame.
sentences.zh: 指控她们可以了结恩怨或者转移责备。

sentences.en: Once it started, it snowballed; people piled on, afraid of being accused themselves if they didn’t join in.
sentences.zh: 一旦开始，它就像滚雪球一样越滚越大；人们纷纷加入，生怕自己如果不随大流也会被指控。

sentences.en: So, which is it? Maybe a bit of all three: some sickness, a lot of fear, and plenty of human messiness.
sentences.zh: 所以，到底是因为什么？也许上述三者兼而有之：一些疾病，满腔恐惧，再加上一堆剪不断理还乱的人性纷争。

sentences.en: Now, to wrap things up, this was a weird period indeed.
sentences.zh: 好了，总结一下，这确实是一个奇特的时期。

sentences.en: 15 months, more than 200 people accused, the vast majority of whom were women.
sentences.zh: 15个月里，超过200人被指控，其中绝大多数是女性。

sentences.en: Nineteen people were hanged, one eighty-year-old man crushed to death under heavy stones, and at least five more died in jail.
sentences.zh: 十九人被绞死，一个八十岁的老人被重石压死，至少还有五人死在狱中。

sentences.en: It was a miscarriage of justice indeed, and to think, it might all have come down to bad bread.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场冤假错案，仔细想想，这一切竟然可能只是因为坏了的面包。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the Salem Witch Trials.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于塞勒姆审巫案的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目足够有趣，也希望你们学到了新知识。

sentences.en: If you enjoyed it, we have another episode on the history of witches, it’s episode number 322.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢本期节目，我们还有另一集关于女巫历史的节目，那是第322期。

sentences.en: I'll put a link in the show notes if you'd like to listen to that one.
sentences.zh: 如果你想听那一期，我会在节目文稿里放一个链接。

sentences.en: And we have a bunch of other “horror”-themed episodes, or ones about “weird history” too.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一堆其他以“恐怖”为主题的节目，或者关于“猎奇历史”的节目。

sentences.en: Just click on the “horror” or “weird history” tab if you’re listening on our website, and I’ll put some links to all of those in the show notes as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在我们的网站上收听，只需点击“恐怖”或“猎奇历史”标签即可，我也会把所有这些链接放在节目文稿中。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是阿莱斯特·巴奇，大家注意安全，我们下期节目见。
